title: Fever in a child: how to measure and when to see a doctor
what: How to measure a child's temperature correctly, when to lower it, and when to call a doctor urgently.
why: When your child feels hot, limp, or fussy, or you suspect they are sick.
duration: measuring takes from a few seconds to a few minutes, depending on the thermometer
tell_doctor: How many days the fever has lasted and how high it goes
Which fever reducer and what dose you gave, and when
Whether your child is drinking and how many times they urinated
Whether there is a rash, vomiting, diarrhea, cough, or pain

prepare.title: Thermometer
prepare.text: An electronic one is easiest. A mercury one is dangerous if it breaks.

prepare.title: Where to measure
prepare.text: Babies are often measured under the arm or in the ear. How to do it right is in your thermometer's instructions.

prepare.title: Medicine
prepare.text: Use only a children's fever reducer, in a dose based on your child's weight. Check the dose with your pediatrician.

prepare.title: Fluids
prepare.text: With a fever, your child needs to drink more.

bring: A list of questions for the pediatrician
steps: Wait 15 to 20 minutes after running, eating, or a bath
Wipe the armpit with a dry cloth
Put the thermometer in the armpit and hold your child's arm against the body
Hold until the beep or as long as the instructions say
Write down the time and the number
Undress your child, do not bundle them up
Offer drinks more often, in small amounts
feel: Your child may be fussy and eat poorly, which is usual with a fever
How your child behaves matters more than the exact number
after: If your child plays and drinks, you can usually watch them and call the pediatrician
A fever reducer is more often given when the child feels bad, not just by the number, so check with your pediatrician
Do not rub with alcohol or vinegar
Measure again 30 to 60 minutes after the medicine
red_flags: Your child is under 3 months old with a temperature of 38°C (100.4°F) or higher: call emergency services or the pediatrician right away
A seizure, your child will not wake up, or is very limp: call emergency services
A rash that does not fade when pressed with a glass: call emergency services
Trouble breathing, not drinking, or no urine for more than 6 to 8 hours: call emergency services

faq.q: At what number should I bring the temperature down?
faq.a: Usually the focus is on how your child feels, not only the number. Your pediatrician can tell you exactly for your child.

faq.q: Can I bathe a child with a fever?
faq.a: A warm shower is usually fine if your child does not feel very ill. Do not cool with cold water or rubdowns.

reminders.text: Take your child's temperature and write it down. Offer something to drink.
